questions.stem: A 32-year-old G1P0 woman at 35 weeks gestation is receiving intravenous magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis due to severe preeclampsia. After several hours of infusion, she becomes lethargic and has diminished deep tendon reflexes. Her respiratory rate is 10/min. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Increase the magnesium sulfate infusion rate
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Increasing magnesium sulfate worsens toxicity and risks respiratory or cardiac arrest.
Correct: Intravenous calcium gluconate is the immediate antidote for magnesium sulfate toxicity (lethargy, hyporeflexia, respiratory depression).
Incorrect: Antihypertensives do not reverse magnesium toxicity.
Incorrect: Furosemide promotes renal excretion but is not the acute first-line antidote for magnesium toxicity.
Incorrect: Observing without treatment risks progression to respiratory arrest.
questions.explanation: Administer intravenous calcium gluconate Explanation: • Loss of deep tendon reflexes, lethargy, and respiratory depression signal magnesium sulfate toxicity, and calcium gluconate is the antidote. • Monitor respiratory rate, urine output, patellar reflexes, and serum magnesium, especially with renal impairment. • Increasing the infusion worsens toxicity, furosemide is not first line, and observation alone risks respiratory arrest.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which immunohistochemical marker predicts response to trastuzumab therapy?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: ER (estrogen receptor) predicts response to endocrine therapy (e.g., tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors), not trastuzumab.
Incorrect: PR (progesterone receptor) is a hormone receptor marker predicting endocrine therapy response, not trastuzumab.
Correct: HER2/neu overexpression/amplification predicts response to trastuzumab (Herceptin), a monoclonal antibody targeting HER2.
Incorrect: Ki-67 is a proliferation index marker, not the target of trastuzumab.
Incorrect: p53 is a tumor suppressor marker and does not predict trastuzumab response.
questions.explanation: HER2/neu Explanation: • HER2/neu overexpression/amplification predicts response to trastuzumab (Herceptin), a monoclonal antibody targeting HER2. • ER and PR predict response to endocrine therapy, while HER2 status is assessed by immunohistochemistry or FISH.

questions.case_context: A 33-year-old woman presents with seven months of amenorrhea following a spontaneous abortion. She underwent dilation and curettage (D&C) at that time. Her past medical and surgical history is unremarkable. Menarche occurred at age 11, and her cycles were previously regular every 28–30 days. Physical examination is normal, pregnancy test is negative.
questions.stem: What is the most likely diagnosis?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Premature ovarian insufficiency presents with elevated FSH and hypoestrogenism without a preceding D&C history.
Correct: Asherman syndrome (intrauterine adhesions) classically causes secondary amenorrhea after uterine instrumentation such as D&C following pregnancy loss.
Incorrect: Hyperprolactinemia typically causes galactorrhea and amenorrhea due to pituitary/medication causes, not post-D&C scarring.
Incorrect: Hypothyroidism causes systemic symptoms and abnormal thyroid function, neither of which is present here.
questions.explanation: Asherman syndrome (intrauterine adhesions) • Asherman syndrome occurs when intrauterine adhesions form after procedures like D&C, especially following pregnancy loss. These adhesions prevent normal endometrial regeneration, leading to secondary amenorrhea. Physical exam and hormonal profile are often normal. Explanation: A. Premature ovarian insufficiency • This condition causes amenorrhea due to ovarian failure before age 40, usually associated with elevated FSH and low estrogen. There is no history or lab evidence of ovarian failure here. C. Hyperprolactinemia • Elevated prolactin can cause amenorrhea and galactorrhea. This patient has no breast discharge and no symptoms suggesting pituitary involvement. D. Hypothyroidism • Thyroid dysfunction can cause menstrual irregularities, but the thyroid exam is normal, and there are no systemic symptoms of hypothyroidism.

questions.case_context: A 33-year-old woman presents with seven months of amenorrhea following a spontaneous abortion. She underwent dilation and curettage (D&C) at that time. Her past medical and surgical history is unremarkable. Menarche occurred at age 11, and her cycles were previously regular every 28–30 days. Physical examination is normal, pregnancy test is negative.
questions.stem: Which is the best test to confirm the diagnosis?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: FSH and LH are normal in Asherman syndrome because the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis is intact.
Correct: Hysterosalpingography (HSG) outlines the uterine cavity with contrast to confirm intrauterine adhesions/obliteration (hysteroscopy is gold standard).
Incorrect: Routine pelvic ultrasound is less sensitive than HSG or hysteroscopy for demonstrating intrauterine synechiae.
Incorrect: A progesterone challenge test localizes outflow/endometrial vs. anovulatory causes but does not directly confirm intrauterine adhesions.
questions.explanation: Hysterosalpingography (HSG) Explanation: • HSG is an imaging test that outlines the uterine cavity and fallopian tubes using contrast. In Asherman syndrome, it reveals intrauterine adhesions or obliteration of the cavity. • Hysteroscopy is considered the gold standard because it allows direct visualization and treatment, but HSG is commonly used as a confirmatory diagnostic test.

questions.case_context: A 33-year-old woman presents with seven months of amenorrhea following a spontaneous abortion. She underwent dilation and curettage (D&C) at that time. Her past medical and surgical history is unremarkable. Menarche occurred at age 11, and her cycles were previously regular every 28–30 days. Physical examination is normal, pregnancy test is negative.
questions.stem: What would be the patient’s response if a progestin challenge is administered?
options: Irregular spotting occurs for several weeks
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Withdrawal bleeding occurs only when an intact endometrium has been primed by estrogen.
Correct: In Asherman syndrome, endometrial scarring prevents response to progestin, so no withdrawal bleeding occurs.
Incorrect: Heavy immediate withdrawal bleeding does not occur with a scarred, non-responsive endometrium.
Incorrect: Irregular spotting for weeks is not the expected response to a progestin challenge in Asherman syndrome.
questions.explanation: No withdrawal bleeding occurs Explanation: • In Asherman syndrome, the endometrium is scarred and cannot respond to hormonal stimulation. Therefore, after a progestin challenge, there is no withdrawal bleeding, indicating an outflow tract problem or endometrial damage rather than hormonal deficiency.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman presents with a firm, mobile breast mass. The patient undergoes excision of the mass which grossly looks like a white-yellow, well-demarcated nodule with solid smooth cut section. Histology shows a biphasic tumor composed of stromal and epithelial components. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Phyllodes tumor is a fibroepithelial tumor that is typically larger, occurs in older women, and shows leaf-like stromal projections.
Correct: Fibroadenoma is a benign, firm, mobile biphasic (stromal + epithelial) breast mass classically seen in young women with a well-demarcated white-yellow cut surface.
Incorrect: Radial scar is a stellate lesion with central sclerosis that mimics invasive carcinoma on imaging.
Incorrect: Intraductal papilloma typically presents with bloody nipple discharge and fibrovascular cores lined by epithelium.
Incorrect: Medullary carcinoma is an invasive carcinoma characterized by syncytial sheets of pleomorphic cells and a prominent lymphocytic infiltrate.
questions.explanation: Fibroadenoma Explanation: • Fibroadenoma is a benign, firm, mobile biphasic (stromal + epithelial) breast mass classically seen in young women with a well-demarcated white-yellow cut surface. • Phyllodes tumor is also biphasic but is usually larger with leaf-like architecture and a hypercellular stroma.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy has a testicular mass. Histology shows Schiller-Duval bodies. Which immunohistochemical marker is most likely positive?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: β-hCG is elevated in choriocarcinoma (syncytiotrophoblasts) and occasionally seminoma, not yolk sac tumor.
Correct: Schiller-Duval bodies are pathognomonic for yolk sac (endodermal sinus) tumor, which is AFP-positive and the most common testicular tumor in young boys.
Incorrect: CD117 (c-KIT) is classically positive in seminoma/dysgerminoma, not yolk sac tumor.
Incorrect: Inhibin is a marker for sex cord–stromal tumors (Sertoli or Leydig cell tumors), not yolk sac tumor.
Incorrect: CK20 is an epithelial marker used for gastrointestinal/Merkel cell tumors, not testicular yolk sac tumor.
questions.explanation: AFP Explanation: • Schiller-Duval bodies are pathognomonic for yolk sac (endodermal sinus) tumor, which is AFP-positive and the most common testicular tumor in young boys. • β-hCG marks choriocarcinoma and CD117 marks seminoma, while inhibin marks sex cord stromal tumors.

questions.stem: What is the typical order of appearance of secondary sexual characteristics in females during puberty?
options: Pubic hair, breast development, growth spurt
Breast development, pubic hair, growth spurt
Growth spurt, breast development, pubic hair
Pubic hair, growth spurt, breast development
choice_rationales: Incorrect: In most girls, breast budding (thelarche) appears before pubic hair (pubarche).
Correct: Female puberty typically progresses from thelarche to pubarche and then the peak growth spurt.
Incorrect: The growth spurt occurs in mid puberty, after breast development has begun, and is not the first event.
Incorrect: Breast development is typically the first sign of puberty, so it does not come last.
questions.explanation: Breast development, pubic hair, growth spurt Explanation: • In most girls, puberty begins with breast development (thelarche), followed by pubic hair (pubarche), and then the peak growth spurt. • Menarche usually occurs after the peak growth spurt.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman presents with a well-circumscribed breast mass. Histology shows islands of tumor cells floating in pools of mucin. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Medullary carcinoma shows sheets of high-grade cells with pushing borders and a dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, not mucin pools.
Incorrect: Tubular carcinoma is composed of well-formed angulated tubules infiltrating stroma without mucin lakes.
Correct: Mucinous (colloid) carcinoma presents in older women as a well-circumscribed mass with islands of tumor cells floating in abundant extracellular mucin.
Incorrect: Invasive lobular carcinoma shows dyscohesive cells in a single-file ('Indian file') pattern.
Incorrect: DCIS is confined within intact basement membranes of mammary ducts.
questions.explanation: Mucinous carcinoma Explanation: • Mucinous (colloid) carcinoma presents in older women as a well-circumscribed mass with islands of tumor cells floating in abundant extracellular mucin. • Mucinous carcinoma has a better prognosis than most invasive ductal carcinomas.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which testicular condition is associated with increased risk of germ cell tumors?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Hydrocele is a benign fluid collection in the tunica vaginalis and does not increase germ cell tumor risk.
Incorrect: Varicocele is dilation of the pampiniform plexus and is associated with subfertility, not germ cell tumors.
Correct: Cryptorchidism (undescended testis) is a major risk factor for testicular germ cell tumors (especially seminoma).
Incorrect: Epididymitis is an infectious/inflammatory condition without malignant predisposition.
Incorrect: Testicular torsion is an acute vascular emergency, not a neoplasm risk factor.
questions.explanation: Cryptorchidism Explanation: • Cryptorchidism (undescended testis) is a major risk factor for testicular germ cell tumors (especially seminoma). • Orchiopexy lowers but does not remove the risk, and the contralateral testis is also at increased risk.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old G1P0 woman at 28 weeks gestation presents with new-onset hypertension and proteinuria. She is diagnosed with preeclampsia. Which of the following best describes a proposed underlying mechanism contributing to the development of preeclampsia?
options: Increased maternal insulin resistance leading to hyperglycemia
Abnormal placental implantation resulting in endothelial dysfunction
Excessive maternal weight gain causing increased cardiac output
Fetal chromosomal abnormalities leading to placental insufficiency
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Insulin resistance is linked to gestational diabetes rather than the primary pathogenesis of preeclampsia.
Correct: Preeclampsia is driven by abnormal spiral artery remodeling/placental implantation causing placental hypoperfusion and systemic endothelial dysfunction.
Incorrect: Weight gain and increased cardiac output are not the primary mechanism of preeclampsia.
Incorrect: Autoimmune trophoblast destruction is not the proposed mechanism of preeclampsia.
Incorrect: Fetal chromosomal abnormalities are not the general underlying mechanism of preeclampsia.
questions.explanation: Abnormal placental implantation resulting in endothelial dysfunction Explanation: Preeclampsia is believed to originate from abnormal placental development, particularly inadequate trophoblastic invasion of the spiral arteries, leading to poor placental perfusion. This triggers systemic endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and an imbalance of angiogenic and antiangiogenic factors, contributing to hypertension and multi-organ involvement.

questions.stem: Which hormone is primarily responsible for the initiation of puberty in both males and females?
choice_rationales: Correct: Increased pulsatile GnRH secretion from the hypothalamus initiates puberty in both sexes.
Incorrect: FSH is released in response to GnRH and acts on the gonads, so it is downstream of the initiating signal.
Incorrect: LH is released in response to GnRH and acts on the gonads, so it is downstream of the initiating signal.
Incorrect: Prolactin regulates lactation and is not the trigger for pubertal onset.
questions.explanation: Gonadotropin releasing hormone (GnRH) Explanation: • Puberty begins when pulsatile GnRH secretion from the hypothalamus increases. • GnRH stimulates the pituitary to release LH and FSH, which then activate the gonads. • LH and FSH act downstream of GnRH, and prolactin is not a primary initiator of puberty.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which is the most common testicular neoplasm in men over 60 years?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Seminoma peaks in men aged 30–40 years, not >60 years.
Incorrect: Embryonal carcinoma occurs primarily in young men (20–30 years).
Correct: Testicular lymphoma (most often diffuse large B-cell lymphoma) is the most common testicular neoplasm in men over 60.
Incorrect: Leydig cell tumors are uncommon sex cord–stromal tumors, not the most common neoplasm >60.
Incorrect: Testicular teratomas occur primarily in infants/children or young adult men.
questions.explanation: Lymphoma Explanation: • Testicular lymphoma (most often diffuse large B-cell lymphoma) is the most common testicular neoplasm in men over 60. • Germ cell tumors such as seminoma peak in young men, while lymphoma and spermatocytic tumor occur in older men.

questions.case_context: A 25-year-old woman presents with a six-month history of amenorrhea. Her pregnancy test is negative. She is evaluated for other causes of secondary amenorrhea and is given a diagnosis of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).
questions.stem: Which of the following is consistent with this disorder?
options: A history of regular menses each month prior to six months
choice_rationales: Incorrect: PCOS causes normal or unopposed estrogen levels rather than estrogen deficiency and vaginal atrophy.
Incorrect: Osteoporosis is associated with hypoestrogenic states (e.g., POI), not PCOS.
Correct: Chronic anovulation in PCOS leads to unopposed estrogen stimulation of the endometrium, increasing the risk of endometrial hyperplasia.
Incorrect: PCOS is associated with insulin resistance and hyperglycemia, not hypoglycemia.
Incorrect: PCOS typically presents with chronic oligomenorrhea/irregular menses rather than previously regular monthly cycles.
questions.explanation: Endometrial hyperplasia Explanation: • PCOS is characterized by chronic anovulation, leading to unopposed estrogen exposure on the endometrium, which increases the risk of endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma. • A is incorrect because estrogen levels are not deficient; they are often normal or slightly elevated. • B is incorrect because osteoporosis is associated with hypoestrogenism, not PCOS. • D is incorrect because PCOS is linked to insulin resistance and hyperglycemia, not hypoglycemia. • E is incorrect because PCOS typically involves a history of irregular cycles, not previously regular menses.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: A 43-year-old woman has noted menstrual periods that have been exceptionally heavy, lasting 6 to 8 days, for 4 months. She has also noted minor intermenstrual bleeding. On physical examination her uterine cervix appears normal, and a Pap smear shows no abnormal cells. Pelvic examination reveals that the uterus is enlarged to twice normal size and is nodular. There are no adnexal masses. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Endometrial carcinoma typically presents with postmenopausal bleeding and does not characteristically cause a uniformly nodular enlarged uterus.
Correct: Leiomyomata (uterine fibroids) present in reproductive-aged women with heavy/prolonged menstrual bleeding and an enlarged, nodular uterus.
Incorrect: Ectopic pregnancy presents acutely with pain, positive pregnancy test, and adnexal findings.
Incorrect: Endometriosis typically causes dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, and pelvic pain rather than a large nodular uterus.
Incorrect: Secondary syphilis presents with systemic mucocutaneous lesions, not a nodular enlarged uterus.
questions.explanation: Leiomyomata Explanation: • Heavy, prolonged menses with intermenstrual bleeding and an enlarged, nodular uterus in a woman in her 40s are typical of uterine leiomyomas (fibroids). • A normal cervix, a normal Pap smear, and no adnexal masses make cervical disease and an adnexal process less likely. • Endometrial carcinoma usually presents with postmenopausal bleeding, and endometriosis causes pain rather than a nodular uterus.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old G1P0 woman at 33 weeks gestation is admitted with severe preeclampsia. She is started on intravenous magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis. Which of the following best describes the primary mechanism by which magnesium sulfate prevents eclamptic seizures?
options: Reduction of systemic blood pressure via vasodilation
Antagonism of NMDA receptors and calcium channels in the central nervous system
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Magnesium sulfate does not act primarily by inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis.
Incorrect: Magnesium sulfate is not a primary systemic antihypertensive agent.
Correct: Magnesium sulfate prevents eclamptic seizures mainly via central nervous system NMDA receptor antagonism and calcium channel blockade.
Incorrect: Enhancing GABAergic neurotransmission is the mechanism of benzodiazepines, not magnesium sulfate.
Incorrect: Platelet aggregation inhibition is not the mechanism of seizure prophylaxis.
questions.explanation: Antagonism of NMDA receptors and calcium channels in the central nervous system Explanation: Magnesium sulfate prevents eclamptic seizures primarily through central nervous system depression by: • Blocking NMDA receptors, which reduces neuronal excitability • Antagonizing calcium influx, which helps prevent cerebral vasospasm and neuronal injury • Stabilizing the blood-brain barrier, reducing cerebral edema • Promoting vasodilation, especially in cerebral vessels, which may reduce ischemia and prevent seizure activity. It is not an antihypertensive agent and does not directly affect prostaglandin synthesis or platelet aggregation.

questions.case_context: A 16-year-old girl presents with primary amenorrhea and no breast development. Physical exam shows scant axillary and pubic hair, no palpable uterus, short vagina, and no cervix. Pelvic ultrasound reveals undescended testes and no uterus or ovaries. Karyotype: 46, XY.
questions.stem: What is this patient’s syndrome?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Turner syndrome has a 45,X karyotype with streak ovaries and a present (hypoplastic) uterus.
Incorrect: Müllerian agenesis has a 46,XX karyotype and normal ovaries.

Correct: Complete androgen insensitivity syndrome (CAIS) presents in a phenotypic female with 46,XY karyotype, undescended testes, absent uterus, short blind vaginal pouch, and scant pubic/axillary hair.
Incorrect: Hypothalamic amenorrhea has normal 46,XX female anatomy and uterus.
questions.explanation: Complete androgen insensitivity syndrome Explanation: • A phenotypic female with a 46,XY karyotype, undescended testes, no uterus, a short blind vagina, and scant pubic and axillary hair has complete androgen insensitivity syndrome (CAIS). • Turner syndrome is 45,X with streak ovaries, and Müllerian agenesis is 46,XX with normal ovaries and normal pubic hair.

questions.case_context: A 16-year-old girl presents with primary amenorrhea and no breast development. Physical exam shows scant axillary and pubic hair, no palpable uterus, short vagina, and no cervix. Pelvic ultrasound reveals undescended testes and no uterus or ovaries. Karyotype: 46, XY.
questions.stem: What is the cause of the syndrome?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Aromatase mutation causes estrogen deficiency and virilization, not CAIS.
Correct: CAIS is caused by an X-linked loss-of-function mutation in the androgen receptor gene.
Incorrect: AMH deficiency results in persistent Müllerian duct structures (uterus/tubes) in an XY individual.
Incorrect: Testosterone production is normal or elevated in CAIS; target tissues simply cannot respond.
questions.explanation: Mutation in androgen receptor gene Explanation: • CAIS is caused by an X-linked loss-of-function mutation in the androgen receptor gene. • Complete androgen insensitivity is 46,XY with normal testes and female external genitalia.

questions.case_context: A 16-year-old girl presents with primary amenorrhea and no breast development. Physical exam shows scant axillary and pubic hair, no palpable uterus, short vagina, and no cervix. Pelvic ultrasound reveals undescended testes and no uterus or ovaries. Karyotype: 46, XY.
questions.stem: Why does this patient have a vaginal pouch?
options: Regression of Müllerian ducts due to AMH
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Lack of estrogen stimulation does not cause absence of the uterus and upper vagina.
Correct: Sertoli cells in the testes secrete anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), causing regression of the Müllerian ducts (no uterus/upper vagina), leaving a short urogenital-sinus vaginal pouch.
Incorrect: Failure of Wolffian duct development explains absent male internal structures (epididymis/vas), not the vaginal pouch itself.
Incorrect: Incomplete Müllerian fusion produces uterine anomalies (e.g., septate/bicornuate uterus), not complete absence.
questions.explanation: Regression of Müllerian ducts due to AMH Explanation: • Sertoli cells in the testes secrete anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), causing regression of the Müllerian ducts (no uterus/upper vagina), leaving a short urogenital-sinus vaginal pouch. • The uterus, fallopian tubes, and upper vagina are absent, so the vagina ends as a blind pouch.

questions.case_context: A 16-year-old girl presents with primary amenorrhea and no breast development. Physical exam shows scant axillary and pubic hair, no palpable uterus, short vagina, and no cervix. Pelvic ultrasound reveals undescended testes and no uterus or ovaries. Karyotype: 46, XY.
questions.stem: Why does this patient have no pubic or axillary hair?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Pubic and axillary hair growth is driven by androgens, not estrogen.
Correct: Defective androgen receptors prevent hair follicles from responding to testosterone and adrenal androgens, resulting in scant/absent pubic and axillary hair.
Incorrect: Progesterone does not drive pubic or axillary hair development.
Incorrect: Adrenal glands still produce androgens normally in CAIS; the receptors are nonfunctional.
questions.explanation: Lack of androgen receptor function Explanation: • Defective androgen receptors prevent hair follicles from responding to testosterone and adrenal androgens, resulting in scant/absent pubic and axillary hair. • Pubic and axillary hair depend on androgen receptor signaling, so hair is sparse even though androgen levels are normal or high.

questions.case_context: A 16-year-old girl presents with primary amenorrhea and no breast development. Physical exam shows scant axillary and pubic hair, no palpable uterus, short vagina, and no cervix. Pelvic ultrasound reveals undescended testes and no uterus or ovaries. Karyotype: 46, XY.
questions.stem: Will testosterone levels be low or high in this patient?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Testosterone levels are not low because Leydig cells function normally.
Incorrect: Testosterone levels exceed the normal female range.
Correct: Testosterone levels are in the normal to high male range because the testes produce testosterone without negative feedback from functional androgen receptors.
Incorrect: Testosterone is readily detectable at male-range levels.
questions.explanation: High (normal male range) Explanation: • Testosterone levels are in the normal to high male range because the testes produce testosterone without negative feedback from functional androgen receptors. • Estrogen is also raised from peripheral aromatization of testosterone, which explains breast development at puberty.

questions.case_context: A 16-year-old girl presents with primary amenorrhea and no breast development. Physical exam shows scant axillary and pubic hair, no palpable uterus, short vagina, and no cervix. Pelvic ultrasound reveals undescended testes and no uterus or ovaries. Karyotype: 46, XY.
questions.stem: Why should this patient’s testes be removed?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Testes are not removed to prevent estrogen excess.
Incorrect: Tissues are already insensitive to androgens, so androgen excess does not cause virilization.
Correct: Undescended testes carry an increased risk of gonadal malignancy (such as seminoma/dysgerminoma) after puberty, so gonadectomy is recommended after pubertal development.
Incorrect: Keeping the testes through puberty actually allows breast development via peripheral aromatization of testosterone to estrogen.
questions.explanation: To prevent gonadal malignancy Explanation: • The undescended testes in complete androgen insensitivity syndrome carry a neoplasia risk (about 22% in the lecture), so they are removed. • Removal is recommended after complete pubertal development, around age 16 to 18, because the testes supply the testosterone that is converted to estrogen for puberty, and hormone replacement follows removal.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about testicular teratoma is correct?
options: Malignant in postpubertal males even if mature
Occurs only as part of mixed GCT
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Postpubertal testicular teratomas are malignant even when histologically mature, unlike prepubertal teratomas.
Correct: In postpubertal males, testicular teratoma is considered malignant and capable of metastasis even if all elements appear histologically mature.
Incorrect: Pure teratomas do not typically elevate β-hCG.
Incorrect: Teratomas can occur in pure form (especially in children) as well as part of mixed germ cell tumors.
Incorrect: Postpubertal testicular teratomas can metastasize.
questions.explanation: Malignant in postpubertal males even if mature Explanation: • In postpubertal males, testicular teratoma is considered malignant and capable of metastasis even if all elements appear histologically mature. • Elevated β-hCG points to choriocarcinoma or syncytiotrophoblastic elements rather than pure teratoma.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which of the following is the single most important prognostic factor in invasive breast carcinoma?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Tumor size is important for T staging, but axillary lymph node status is the single strongest prognostic factor.
Incorrect: Histologic grade provides prognostic information but is secondary to lymph node status.
Correct: Axillary lymph node status (presence and number of nodal metastases) is the single most important prognostic factor in invasive breast carcinoma.
Incorrect: ER/PR status is primarily predictive of endocrine therapy response and secondary for prognosis.
Incorrect: HER2 status guides targeted therapy and prognosis, but nodal status remains the single most important prognostic factor.
questions.explanation: Axillary lymph node status Explanation: • Axillary lymph node status (presence and number of nodal metastases) is the single most important prognostic factor in invasive breast carcinoma. • Tumor size, grade, and ER, PR, and HER2 status add prognostic and predictive information, but nodal status is the strongest single factor.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which vaccine protects against HPV types 16 and 18?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Hepatitis B vaccine protects against HBV, not HPV.
Correct: Gardasil-9 protects against 9 HPV types, including high-risk oncogenic types 16 and 18.
Incorrect: Varivax protects against varicella-zoster virus (chickenpox).
Incorrect: Only Gardasil-9 protects against HPV.
Incorrect: Gardasil-9 is the correct choice.
questions.explanation: Gardasil-9 Explanation: • Gardasil-9 is the 9-valent HPV vaccine that protects against the high risk types 16 and 18 as well as other types including 6 and 11. • Hepatitis B vaccine and Varivax target hepatitis B virus and varicella zoster virus, so neither covers HPV.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman at 20 weeks gestation comes for a routine prenatal visit. Her blood pressure today is 100/60 mmHg, which is lower than her pre-pregnancy baseline of 115/70 mmHg. She is asymptomatic. Which of the following best explains this finding?
options: Increased systemic vascular resistance due to progesterone
Decreased cardiac output due to reduced plasma volume
Increased venous return due to uterine compression
Decreased systemic vascular resistance due to hormonal changes
Increased blood pressure due to elevated renin-angiotensin activity
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Systemic vascular resistance decreases (rather than increases) during normal pregnancy.
Incorrect: Both cardiac output and plasma volume increase during pregnancy.
Incorrect: Uterine compression of the IVC decreases venous return in later pregnancy.
Correct: Progesterone and vasodilatory mediators lower systemic vascular resistance, causing physiologic blood pressure decline in the first and second trimesters.
Incorrect: Despite RAAS activation, systemic vasodilation predominates so BP decreases in mid-pregnancy.
questions.explanation: Decreased systemic vascular resistance due to hormonal changes Explanation: • During early pregnancy, progesterone and other vasodilatory factors cause decreased systemic vascular resistance, leading to a drop in blood pressure in the first and second trimesters. • Cardiac output increases due to higher stroke volume and heart rate. • Plasma volume expands, not decreases. • Venous return is reduced later in pregnancy due to uterine compression, not increased. • Renin-angiotensin activity rises, but systemic vasodilation predominates, so BP falls initially and returns to baseline later.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: A mammogram shows branching linear calcifications. Biopsy reveals malignant cells confined within ducts without invasion. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: LCIS is typically an incidental finding without calcifications and shows monomorphic discohesive cells distending lobules.
Correct: DCIS classically presents on mammography with linear/branching microcalcifications and shows malignant epithelial cells confined within ducts without basement membrane invasion.
Incorrect: Invasive ductal carcinoma penetrates the basement membrane into surrounding stroma.
Incorrect: Paget disease of the breast presents as an eczematous nipple/areolar lesion.
Incorrect: Medullary carcinoma is an invasive carcinoma forming a well-circumscribed mass.
questions.explanation: DCIS Explanation: • DCIS classically presents on mammography with linear/branching microcalcifications and shows malignant epithelial cells confined within ducts without basement membrane invasion. • LCIS is usually an incidental, multifocal finding and does not produce this linear branching calcification pattern.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: A 40-year-old man presents with penile erythematous plaque. A biopsy is done, showing full-thickness dysplasia of the squamous epithelium without invasion. What is the diagnosis?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Condyloma acuminatum is a benign HPV-related papillary lesion with koilocytosis, not full-thickness dysplasia.
Correct: Penile intraepithelial neoplasia (PeIN) is characterized by full-thickness squamous epithelial dysplasia without stromal invasion (carcinoma in situ).
Incorrect: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) shows invasion through the basement membrane.
Incorrect: Balanitis is inflammation of the glans penis without full-thickness dysplasia.
Incorrect: Lichen sclerosus shows epidermal atrophy and dermal homogenization, not full-thickness dysplasia.
questions.explanation: PeIN (penile intraepithelial neoplasm) Explanation: • Penile intraepithelial neoplasia (PeIN) is characterized by full-thickness squamous epithelial dysplasia without stromal invasion (carcinoma in situ). • Invasive squamous cell carcinoma would show stromal invasion, and balanitis and lichen sclerosus lack full-thickness dysplasia.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which of the following is a common site of metastasis for prostate cancer?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Liver is a less common site compared to axial bone/spine.
Incorrect: Lung metastases occur later/less commonly than axial bone metastases.
Incorrect: Brain metastasis is uncommon in prostate cancer.
Correct: Prostate cancer classically metastasizes via Batson venous plexus to the axial skeleton (especially the lumbar spine), producing osteoblastic lesions.
Incorrect: Skin metastasis is rare in prostate cancer.
questions.explanation: Spine Explanation: • Prostate cancer classically metastasizes via Batson venous plexus to the axial skeleton (especially the lumbar spine), producing osteoblastic lesions. • Prostate metastases are typically osteoblastic and often raise serum alkaline phosphatase.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 18 weeks gestation comes for a routine prenatal visit. Which of the following best describes the normal physiological change in cardiac output during pregnancy?
options: Cardiac output decreases due to reduced stroke volume
Cardiac output remains unchanged throughout pregnancy
Cardiac output decreases due to increased systemic vascular resistance
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Stroke volume and heart rate both increase during pregnancy.
Incorrect: Cardiac output rises substantially during pregnancy.
Incorrect: A 10% increase underestimates the physiologic rise in pregnancy.
Correct: Cardiac output increases by approximately 30–50% during pregnancy due to increased stroke volume and heart rate.
Incorrect: Systemic vascular resistance decreases during pregnancy, and cardiac output increases.
questions.explanation: Cardiac output increases by approximately 30–50% Explanation: • During pregnancy, cardiac output rises significantly (30–50%), primarily due to increased stroke volume and heart rate. • This supports increased metabolic demands and uteroplacental circulation. • Systemic vascular resistance decreases due to progesterone-mediated vasodilation, so blood pressure falls slightly in early pregnancy despite higher cardiac output.

questions.case_context: A 17-year-old adolescent presents with primary amenorrhea. She has normal breast development but scant pubic and axillary hair. Pelvic ultrasound shows absence of the uterus.
questions.stem: Which of the following is the most likely karyotype?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: 46,XX with absent uterus would be Müllerian agenesis, which has normal pubic/axillary hair.
Incorrect: 45,X (Turner syndrome) presents with absent breast development and a present uterus.
Correct: Primary amenorrhea with normal breasts, scant pubic/axillary hair, and absent uterus is classic for androgen insensitivity syndrome (46,XY).
Incorrect: Mosaic 45,X/46,XX presents as a Turner spectrum phenotype with a uterus present.
questions.explanation: 46, XY Explanation: • Primary amenorrhea with normal breasts, scant pubic and axillary hair, and an absent uterus is classic for androgen insensitivity syndrome, which is 46,XY. • 46,XX with an absent uterus would be Müllerian agenesis with normal pubic hair, and 45,X Turner syndrome lacks breast development and has a uterus.

questions.case_context: A 17-year-old adolescent presents with primary amenorrhea. She has normal breast development but scant pubic and axillary hair. Pelvic ultrasound shows absence of the uterus.
questions.stem: Which of the following is the best explanation for breast development in a patient with androgen insensitivity?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Testes primarily produce androgens (testosterone), not large amounts of estrogen directly.
Incorrect: Adrenal glands produce minimal estrogen.
Incorrect: Breast development is driven by estrogen, not progesterone.
Correct: High circulating testosterone is peripherally converted to estradiol via aromatase, driving normal breast development in AIS.
Incorrect: Breast tissue does not autonomously synthesize estrogen to drive pubertal development.
questions.explanation: Peripheral conversion of androgens Explanation: • In androgen insensitivity syndrome (AIS), the patient has testes that produce testosterone, but androgen receptors are defective. • Testosterone is converted to estradiol via aromatase in peripheral tissues, leading to breast development despite lack of androgen action. • A is incorrect because gonads (testes) primarily produce androgens, not estrogens. • B is incorrect because adrenal glands produce minimal estrogen. • C is incorrect because progesterone does not drive breast development. • E is incorrect because breast tissue does not autonomously produce estrogen.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which histologic feature is characteristic of invasive lobular carcinoma?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Tubule formation is characteristic of well-differentiated invasive ductal/tubular carcinoma.
Correct: Invasive lobular carcinoma classically shows dyscohesive tumor cells arranged in single-file ('Indian file') strands due to loss of E-cadherin.
Incorrect: Cribriform architecture is typical of cribriform DCIS or adenoid cystic/cribriform carcinoma.
Incorrect: Comedo necrosis is characteristic of high-grade comedo DCIS.
Incorrect: Papillary projections characterize papillary neoplasms.
questions.explanation: Indian file pattern Explanation: • Invasive lobular carcinoma classically shows dyscohesive tumor cells arranged in single-file ('Indian file') strands due to loss of E-cadherin. • Tubule formation, cribriform architecture, and comedo necrosis point to ductal lesions rather than lobular carcinoma.

questions.stem: Chronic severe illness can delay puberty by what mechanism?
options: Suppression of estrogen production in the ovary and testosterone in the testicles
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Gonadal hormone production falls as a consequence of reduced LH and FSH, but the primary suppression is at the hypothalamus.
Incorrect: LH production falls, but this results from reduced GnRH rather than being the primary mechanism.
Correct: Chronic illness suppresses hypothalamic GnRH secretion, which delays puberty.
Incorrect: Continuous (non pulsatile) GnRH stimulation desensitizes the pituitary, as with GnRH agonist therapy, but chronic illness reduces GnRH secretion rather than increasing it.
questions.explanation: Suppression of GnRH secretion Explanation: • Chronic illness, undernutrition, and low energy availability suppress hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility. • Reduced GnRH lowers LH and FSH, causing functional hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and delayed puberty. • The defect is central, and the low gonadal hormone levels are a downstream result.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which of the following is true regarding spermatocytic tumor?
options: Associated with intratubular germ cell neoplasia
Occurs in older men and is indolent
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Classic seminoma occurs in young men (15–40); spermatocytic tumor occurs in older men (>50).
Incorrect: Unlike classic seminoma, spermatocytic tumor is NOT associated with germ cell neoplasia in situ (ITGCN).
Incorrect: Spermatocytic tumor is indolent with an excellent prognosis and rarely metastasizes.
Correct: Spermatocytic tumor occurs in older men, lacks ITGCN association, and follows an indolent clinical course.
Incorrect: Orchiectomy alone is typically curative without chemotherapy.
questions.explanation: Occurs in older men and is indolent Explanation: • Spermatocytic tumor occurs in older men, lacks ITGCN association, and follows an indolent clinical course. • It does not arise from intratubular germ cell neoplasia and does not typically metastasize, so orchiectomy alone is usually curative.

questions.stem: A child with short straight scant pubic hair should be characterized as
choice_rationales: Correct: Short, straight, scant pubic hair is characteristic of Tanner stage 2.
Incorrect: Stage 3 hair is darker, coarser, and curlier and spreads over the mons pubis.
Incorrect: Stage 4 hair is adult type in character but covers a smaller area than in adults.
Incorrect: Stage 5 hair is adult type and spreads to the medial thighs.
questions.explanation: Tanner Stage 2 Explanation: • Tanner stage 1 has no pubic hair. • Stage 2 has sparse, long, slightly pigmented downy hair that is straight or slightly curled. • Stage 3 hair is darker, coarser, and curlier and spreads over the mons pubis. • Stage 4 is adult type hair over a smaller area, and stage 5 is adult type hair that spreads to the medial thighs.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which congenital penile anomaly involves a ventral urethral opening?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Epispadias involves a dorsal urethral opening.
Correct: Hypospadias is a congenital anomaly where the urethral meatus opens on the ventral surface of the penis.
Incorrect: Phimosis is inability to retract the foreskin over the glans.
Incorrect: Paraphimosis is a retracted foreskin trapped behind the glans.
Incorrect: Balanitis is inflammation of the glans penis.
questions.explanation: Hypospadias Explanation: • Hypospadias is a congenital anomaly where the urethral meatus opens on the ventral surface of the penis. • Epispadias is a dorsal urethral opening, and phimosis and paraphimosis involve the foreskin.

questions.stem: Which hormone is responsible for the development of acne during puberty?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Progesterone does not drive the sebaceous gland activity responsible for pubertal acne.
Incorrect: LH stimulates gonadal hormone production but does not act directly on the sebaceous gland.
Incorrect: Estrogen drives breast development and tends to reduce sebum production rather than increase it.
Correct: Androgens stimulate sebaceous glands to increase sebum production, leading to acne.
questions.explanation: Androgens Explanation: • Androgens stimulate sebaceous gland growth and sebum production and promote follicular plugging, which leads to comedones and acne. • The rise in adrenal and gonadal androgens at puberty explains why acne typically begins in early adolescence.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which of the following breast lesions carries the highest risk of progression to carcinoma?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Non-proliferative fibrocystic changes carry no significantly increased carcinoma risk.
Incorrect: Usual duct hyperplasia carries only a mild (~1.5–2x) increased risk.
Correct: Atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) carries the highest risk of progression to invasive carcinoma (~4–5x) among the listed lesions.
Incorrect: Solitary intraductal papilloma without atypia carries a much lower risk than ADH.
Incorrect: Typical fibroadenoma does not significantly increase carcinoma risk.
questions.explanation: Atypical ductal hyperplasia Explanation: • Atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) carries the highest risk of progression to invasive carcinoma (~4–5x) among the listed lesions. • Usual duct hyperplasia, fibrocystic changes without atypia, and fibroadenoma carry at most a slight increase in risk.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: A 19-year-old university student notes the sudden onset of severe discomfort in his scrotum late one evening. No position is comfortable for him to sit or lie down. Aspirin and beer have no effect. He has a friend drive him to the emergency room. On physical examination his vital signs include temperature 37°C, respirations 22/minute, pulse 80/minute, and blood pressure 100/65 mm Hg. His left testis is slightly enlarged and exquisitely tender. There is no inguinal adenopathy. A doppler ultrasound scan shows decreased blood flow in the left testis. Which of the following conditions is he most likely to have?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Choriocarcinoma presents as a painless testicular mass or with metastatic symptoms, not acute severe pain with absent blood flow.
Incorrect: Varicocele causes a dull ache ('bag of worms') with preserved arterial flow.
Incorrect: Nephrolithiasis does not reduce intratesticular Doppler blood flow.
Correct: Sudden severe scrotal pain in a young male with an enlarged tender testis and decreased Doppler blood flow is diagnostic of testicular torsion.
Incorrect: Hydrocele is a painless fluid collection that transilluminates with normal blood flow.
questions.explanation: Torsion Explanation: • Sudden severe scrotal pain with an enlarged, exquisitely tender testis and decreased Doppler blood flow is testicular torsion, a surgical emergency. • Varicocele and hydrocele are not acutely painful with absent flow, and choriocarcinoma presents as a painless mass.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old G2P1 woman at 35 weeks gestation presents for routine prenatal care. Her blood pressure is 145/95 mm Hg on two separate readings four hours apart. Urinalysis reveals 1+ protein. She denies headache, visual changes, epigastric pain, or shortness of breath. Laboratory studies show normal platelet count, liver enzymes, and serum creatinine. Fetal growth is appropriate for gestational age, and non-stress test is reactive. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
options: Hospital admission for magnesium sulfate therapy
Outpatient management with close maternal and fetal monitoring
Administration of corticosteroids for fetal lung maturity
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Delivery is indicated at 37 weeks for preeclampsia without severe features, not immediately at 35 weeks when stable.
Incorrect: Magnesium sulfate is reserved for preeclampsia with severe features or eclampsia.
Correct: Preeclampsia without severe features <37 weeks with stable maternal/fetal status is managed expectantly (outpatient with close maternal/fetal monitoring) until 37 weeks.
Incorrect: Antenatal corticosteroids are generally given <34 weeks gestation.
Incorrect: Antihypertensives are reserved for severe-range BP (≥160/110 mmHg), not 145/95 mmHg.
questions.explanation: Outpatient management with close maternal and fetal monitoring Explanation: Preeclampsia without severe features can be managed expectantly if the gestational age is less than 37 weeks, and both maternal and fetal conditions are stable. According to ACOG guidelines: • Outpatient management is appropriate for preeclampsia without severe features. • Monitoring includes: o Weekly maternal labs (CBC, liver enzymes, creatinine) o Weekly amniotic fluid assessment o Fetal growth assessment every 3–4 weeks o Antenatal testing 1–2 times per week o Blood pressure and symptom checks at least weekly o Magnesium sulfate is reserved for preeclampsia with severe features or eclampsia. Delivery is recommended at 37 weeks for preeclampsia without severe features. Corticosteroids are typically used before 34 weeks to promote fetal lung maturity.

questions.case_context: A 15-year-old girl presents with primary amenorrhea and short stature. Physical exam reveals a webbed neck and widely spaced nipples.
questions.stem: Which of the following is the most likely finding on laboratory evaluation?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Low FSH/LH occurs in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, not Turner syndrome.
Correct: Turner syndrome (45,X) causes primary ovarian failure (streak gonads), leading to loss of negative feedback and elevated FSH and LH.
Incorrect: Estradiol is low due to ovarian dysgenesis.
Incorrect: Gonadotropins are markedly elevated, not normal.
questions.explanation: High FSH and LH Explanation: Turner syndrome (45, X) → ovarian failure → high gonadotropins. • Estradiol and progesterone are low because ovaries are nonfunctional.

questions.stem: Which hormone is responsible for breast development in females during puberty?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: LH stimulates ovarian androgen production and triggers ovulation but does not act directly on breast tissue.
Incorrect: Prolactin drives milk production after the breast has been primed by estrogen and progesterone.
Correct: Estrogen is the primary hormone that drives breast development during female puberty.
Incorrect: FSH stimulates ovarian follicle growth and estradiol production but is not the direct stimulus for breast growth.
questions.explanation: Estrogen Explanation: • Ovarian estrogen stimulates growth of ductal tissue, stroma, and fat in the breast, producing thelarche. • Progesterone contributes to lobuloalveolar development later. • Prolactin is needed for lactation and is not the driver of pubertal breast growth.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which ovarian tumor is analogous to seminoma of the testis?
choice_rationales: Correct: Dysgerminoma is the ovarian germ cell tumor histologically and immunophenotypically analogous to testicular seminoma.
Incorrect: Yolk sac tumor occurs in both ovary and testis with the same name.
Incorrect: Embryonal carcinoma occurs in both ovary and testis with the same name.
Incorrect: Granulosa cell tumor is a sex cord–stromal tumor, not analogous to seminoma.
Incorrect: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor is a sex cord–stromal tumor.
questions.explanation: Dysgerminoma Explanation: • Dysgerminoma is the ovarian germ cell tumor histologically and immunophenotypically analogous to testicular seminoma. • Both tumors show sheets of large clear cells separated by fibrous septa containing lymphocytes, and both are radiosensitive.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which histologic feature is diagnostic of condyloma acuminatum?
choice_rationales: Correct: Koilocytosis (perinuclear halo with irregular hyperchromatic 'raisinoid' nuclei) is the hallmark histologic feature of HPV infection in condyloma acuminatum.
Incorrect: Triple M changes (multinucleation, margination, molding) are characteristic of HSV infection.
Incorrect: Call-Exner bodies are characteristic of granulosa cell tumor.
Incorrect: Hobnail cells are seen in clear cell carcinoma.
Incorrect: Schiller-Duval bodies are seen in yolk sac tumor.
questions.explanation: Koilocytosis Explanation: • Koilocytosis (perinuclear halo with irregular hyperchromatic 'raisinoid' nuclei) is the hallmark histologic feature of HPV infection in condyloma acuminatum. • Condyloma acuminatum is caused by low risk HPV types 6 and 11.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which screening method has most reduced cervical cancer mortality?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: HPV DNA testing is a newer primary/co-testing tool, whereas the Pap smear historically produced the dramatic reduction in cervical cancer mortality.
Correct: Widespread Pap smear screening (cervical cytology) has been the primary driver in reducing cervical cancer mortality.
Incorrect: Colposcopy is a diagnostic follow-up procedure, not a population screening method.
Incorrect: Cone biopsy is a diagnostic/therapeutic excisional procedure, not a screening test.
Incorrect: Endocervical curettage is a diagnostic sampling procedure, not a screening method.
questions.explanation: Pap smear Explanation: • Widespread Pap smear screening (cervical cytology) has been the primary driver in reducing cervical cancer mortality. • Colposcopy, cone biopsy, and endocervical curettage are diagnostic or therapeutic procedures rather than screening tests.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which gene mutation is most commonly associated with endometrioid carcinoma?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: TP53 mutations are characteristic of high-grade serous endometrial carcinoma (Type II), not endometrioid.
Correct: PTEN loss-of-function mutation is the most common genetic alteration in endometrioid (Type I) endometrial carcinoma.
Incorrect: BRCA1 mutations are associated with breast and high-grade serous ovarian carcinomas.
Incorrect: KRAS mutations can occur in endometrioid carcinoma, but PTEN is the most common.
Incorrect: RB mutations are classically associated with retinoblastoma and small cell/osteosarcoma.
questions.explanation: PTEN Explanation: • PTEN loss-of-function mutation is the most common genetic alteration in endometrioid (Type I) endometrial carcinoma. • KRAS mutations and mismatch repair defects also occur in endometrioid carcinoma, while TP53 mutation is typical of serous carcinoma.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which of the following is the most important risk factor for endometrial carcinoma?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Multiparity is protective against endometrial carcinoma.
Correct: Obesity is the most important risk factor for endometrial carcinoma due to increased peripheral aromatization of androgens to unopposed estrogen in adipose tissue.
Incorrect: Smoking is not a primary risk factor for endometrial carcinoma (it actually reduces risk via anti-estrogenic effects).
Incorrect: Combined oral contraceptive use reduces endometrial carcinoma risk.
Incorrect: Tubal ligation does not increase endometrial carcinoma risk.
questions.explanation: Obesity Explanation: • Obesity is the most important risk factor for endometrial carcinoma due to increased peripheral aromatization of androgens to unopposed estrogen in adipose tissue. • Other risk factors include nulliparity, early menarche, late menopause, and anovulation, while multiparity and oral contraceptive use are protective.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the first visible sign of female puberty?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: The peak growth spurt occurs in mid puberty, after breast budding has started.
Incorrect: Pubic hair usually appears after breast budding in most girls.
Incorrect: Menarche is a late pubertal event that usually follows thelarche by about 2 to 2.5 years.
Correct: Breast bud development (thelarche) is typically the first visible sign of female puberty.
questions.explanation: Development of breast buds Explanation: • Thelarche, the appearance of breast buds, is usually the first visible sign of puberty in girls. • Pubic hair typically follows, the peak growth spurt occurs in mid puberty, and menarche comes later, often about 2 to 2.5 years after thelarche.

questions.stem: Which of the following hormones is NOT involved in the development of primary sexual characteristics in males during puberty?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Testosterone from Leydig cells is the main hormone driving testicular and genital development in males, so it is involved.
Correct: Estrogen is the main female pubertal sex steroid and is not involved in male primary sexual development.
Incorrect: LH stimulates Leydig cells to produce testosterone, so it is involved.
Incorrect: DHEAS is an adrenal androgen that contributes to androgen effects at puberty, so it is involved.
questions.explanation: Estrogen Explanation: • In males, primary sexual characteristics such as testicular growth, spermatogenesis, and genital growth depend on LH, FSH, testosterone from Leydig cells, and other androgens such as DHEAS. • Estrogen is the main female pubertal sex steroid and is not a driver of male primary sexual development.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old G1P0 woman at 33 weeks gestation presents with severe headache and visual disturbances. Her blood pressure is 170/110 mm Hg. Laboratory studies reveal elevated liver enzymes and thrombocytopenia. Fetal ultrasound shows an estimated fetal weight below the 10th percentile for gestational age. Which of the following is the most likely fetal complication associated with this maternal condition?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Macrosomia is classically associated with maternal diabetes, not preeclampsia.
Incorrect: Neural tube defects are linked to folate deficiency, not preeclampsia.
Correct: Severe preeclampsia causes uteroplacental insufficiency, leading to fetal growth restriction (estimated fetal weight <10th percentile).
Incorrect: Neonatal hyperglycemia is not a classic complication of preeclampsia.
Incorrect: Placental insufficiency more commonly causes oligohydramnios rather than polyhydramnios.
questions.explanation: Fetal growth restriction- Severe preeclampsia is associated with placental insufficiency, which can lead to fetal growth restriction (FGR) due to impaired uteroplacental blood flow. Other fetal complications include: • Preterm birth • Low birth weight • Stillbirth • Neonatal acidosis • Neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission. Macrosomia is more commonly associated with maternal diabetes, not preeclampsia. Neural tube defects are linked to folate deficiency. Polyhydramnios and neonatal hyperglycemia are not typical complications of preeclampsia.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old G2P1 woman at 35 weeks gestation presents with a headache and visual disturbances. Her blood pressure is 162/110 mm Hg. Urinalysis shows 2+ protein. Platelet count is 95,000/mm³. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnosis?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Gestational hypertension lacks proteinuria and severe features.
Incorrect: Chronic hypertension is diagnosed before 20 weeks gestation.
Incorrect: BP ≥160/110, thrombocytopenia (<100,000), headache, and visual changes all define severe features.
Correct: New-onset hypertension ≥160/110 mmHg with proteinuria, thrombocytopenia (<100,000/mm³), headache, and visual disturbances is diagnostic of preeclampsia with severe features.
questions.explanation: Preeclampsia with severe features Explanation: Severe features include BP ≥160/110 mm Hg, thrombocytopenia (<100,000), and symptoms like headache and visual changes. Proteinuria supports the diagnosis.

questions.stem: What factors does NOT influence the timing of puberty?
choice_rationales: Correct: Socioeconomic status is not a direct determinant of puberty timing.
Incorrect: Chronic disease can delay puberty, so it influences timing.
Incorrect: Race and ethnicity influence the typical age of pubertal onset.
Incorrect: Body weight influences timing, with higher body fat associated with earlier onset.
questions.explanation: Socioeconomic status Explanation: • Puberty timing is influenced mainly by genetics, race or ethnicity, body weight and nutrition, and chronic disease. • Socioeconomic status is not a direct biologic determinant of puberty timing and acts, at most, indirectly through nutrition and weight.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman has ascites, right pleural effusion, and an ovarian fibroma. This triad is characteristic of:
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Krukenberg tumor is bilateral ovarian metastasis of mucin-producing signet-ring adenocarcinoma (usually gastric).
Correct: Meigs syndrome is the classic triad of a benign ovarian fibroma, ascites, and right-sided pleural effusion that resolves after tumor resection.
Incorrect: Pseudomyxoma peritonei is intraperitoneal mucin accumulation from mucinous neoplasms.
Incorrect: Gorlin syndrome (nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome) is associated with bilateral ovarian fibromas, not specifically this triad.
Incorrect: Brenner tumor is a benign transitional-cell ovarian tumor.
questions.explanation: Meigs syndrome Explanation: • Meigs syndrome is the classic triad of a benign ovarian fibroma, ascites, and right-sided pleural effusion that resolves after tumor resection. • Krukenberg tumor is metastatic signet ring cell carcinoma, and pseudomyxoma peritonei is mucin collecting in the peritoneum.

questions.stem: In females, what is the primary source of androgen hormones (e.g., testosterone) during puberty?
choice_rationales: Correct: Ovarian theca cells, driven by LH, are the primary source of testosterone in females during puberty.
Incorrect: The adrenal glands release weaker androgens (DHEA and DHEAS) that drive adrenarche, but they are not the primary source of testosterone.
Incorrect: The pituitary gland releases LH and FSH, which stimulate androgen production but are not androgens.
Incorrect: The hypothalamus releases GnRH, which controls the axis but does not make androgens.
questions.explanation: Ovaries Explanation: • During female puberty, ovarian theca cells stimulated by LH produce androgens (androstenedione and testosterone). • Granulosa cells stimulated by FSH convert these androgens to estradiol through aromatase. • The adrenal glands also release weaker androgens (DHEA and DHEAS), but the ovary is the main source of testosterone.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Endometrial hyperplasia with atypia carries what approximate risk of progression to carcinoma?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: <1% is the progression risk for hyperplasia without atypia (simple hyperplasia).
Incorrect: 5% is lower than the actual progression risk for atypical endometrial hyperplasia.
Incorrect: 10% underestimates the risk of progression with atypia.
Correct: Endometrial hyperplasia with atypia carries an approximately 25–50% risk of progression to (or concurrent) endometrial carcinoma.
Incorrect: >75% overestimates the progression risk.
questions.explanation: 25-50% Explanation: • Endometrial hyperplasia with atypia carries an approximately 25–50% risk of progression to (or concurrent) endometrial carcinoma. • The risk of progression is low without atypia and rises with atypia.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which histologic subtype of endometrial carcinoma is the most aggressive?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Endometrioid (Type I) carcinoma is generally well-differentiated with a favorable prognosis.
Correct: Serous endometrial carcinoma (Type II) is the most aggressive histologic subtype, often associated with TP53 mutations and early extrauterine spread.
Incorrect: Mucinous endometrial carcinoma is a lower-grade Type I variant.
Incorrect: Clear cell carcinoma is aggressive, but serous carcinoma is classically the most aggressive prototype.
Incorrect: Adenosquamous carcinoma has a prognosis closer to endometrioid grade.
questions.explanation: Serous Explanation: • Serous endometrial carcinoma (Type II) is the most aggressive histologic subtype, often associated with TP53 mutations and early extrauterine spread. • Endometrioid carcinoma is more common and has a better prognosis, while serous carcinoma arises in atrophic endometrium in older women.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old G2P1 woman at 34 weeks gestation is admitted for management of severe preeclampsia. Her blood pressure is 168/112 mm Hg. The resident considers starting antihypertensive therapy. Which of the following medications is contraindicated in pregnancy and should not be used to treat her hypertension?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: IV labetalol is a first-line agent for acute severe hypertension in pregnancy.
Incorrect: Immediate-release oral nifedipine is a first-line agent for acute severe hypertension in pregnancy.
Incorrect: IV hydralazine is a first-line agent for acute severe hypertension in pregnancy.
Correct: Enalapril (an ACE inhibitor) is contraindicated in pregnancy due to fetal renal dysplasia, oligohydramnios, and teratogenicity.
Incorrect: Methyldopa is safe in pregnancy (though slower acting for chronic control).
questions.explanation: Enalapril Explanation: • ACE inhibitors such as enalapril are contraindicated in pregnancy because they cause fetal renal dysplasia, oligohydramnios, and other teratogenic effects. • IV labetalol, oral nifedipine, IV hydralazine, and methyldopa are all considered safe in pregnancy.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which area of the cervix is most susceptible to HPV infection?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: The endocervical canal is lined by columnar epithelium and is less susceptible than the squamocolumnar junction.
Correct: The transformation zone (squamocolumnar junction undergoing squamous metaplasia) is the area of the cervix most susceptible to HPV infection and neoplasia.
Incorrect: The external os is an anatomic landmark rather than the specific metaplastic zone.
Incorrect: The vaginal fornix is lined by mature stratified squamous epithelium.
Incorrect: The uterine isthmus is above the cervix.
questions.explanation: Transformation zone Explanation: • The transformation zone (squamocolumnar junction undergoing squamous metaplasia) is the area of the cervix most susceptible to HPV infection and neoplasia. • Metaplastic cells in the transformation zone are especially susceptible to high risk HPV types such as 16 and 18.

questions.case_context: A 24-year-old G2P2 woman delivered vaginally eight months ago. Her pregnancy was uncomplicated, but her delivery was complicated by postpartum hemorrhage requiring uterine curettage and transfusion of four units of packed red blood cells. She complains of amenorrhea since delivery. She was unable to breastfeed her baby. She denies headaches, visual changes, or medication use. Pregnancy test is negative.
questions.stem: What is the most likely diagnosis?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Asherman syndrome causes amenorrhea after curettage but does NOT cause inability to breastfeed (prolactin is normal).
Correct: Sheehan syndrome is postpartum pituitary necrosis after severe hemorrhage and hypovolemic shock, presenting with agalactia (low prolactin) and amenorrhea (low gonadotropins).
Incorrect: Premature ovarian insufficiency causes elevated FSH and does not explain acute post-hemorrhage agalactia.
Incorrect: Hypothalamic amenorrhea is a diagnosis of exclusion unrelated to postpartum hemorrhage.
questions.explanation: Sheehan syndrome Explanation: • Sheehan syndrome = postpartum pituitary necrosis due to severe hemorrhage and hypovolemic shock. • Key clues: postpartum hemorrhage, inability to lactate (loss of prolactin), and amenorrhea (loss of gonadotropins).

questions.case_context: A 24-year-old G2P2 woman delivered vaginally eight months ago. Her pregnancy was uncomplicated, but her delivery was complicated by postpartum hemorrhage requiring uterine curettage and transfusion of four units of packed red blood cells. She complains of amenorrhea since delivery. She was unable to breastfeed her baby. She denies headaches, visual changes, or medication use. Pregnancy test is negative.
questions.stem: What is the likely mechanism for the condition?
options: Ischemic necrosis of the anterior pituitary
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Lymphocytic hypophysitis is autoimmune, whereas postpartum hemorrhage causes ischemic infarction.
Correct: Severe postpartum hemorrhage causes hypoperfusion and ischemic necrosis of the enlarged anterior pituitary.
Incorrect: Endometrial scarring causes Asherman syndrome, not agalactia.
Incorrect: Ovarian follicle depletion causes premature ovarian insufficiency.
questions.explanation: Ischemic necrosis of the anterior pituitary Explanation: • Severe blood loss → hypoperfusion → infarction of the anterior pituitary (which enlarges during pregnancy and is more vulnerable to ischemia).

questions.case_context: A 24-year-old G2P2 woman delivered vaginally eight months ago. Her pregnancy was uncomplicated, but her delivery was complicated by postpartum hemorrhage requiring uterine curettage and transfusion of four units of packed red blood cells. She complains of amenorrhea since delivery. She was unable to breastfeed her baby. She denies headaches, visual changes, or medication use. Pregnancy test is negative.
questions.stem: What are other complications that are likely with this condition?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Loss of TSH causes central hypothyroidism, not hyperthyroidism.
Correct: Loss of ACTH from anterior pituitary necrosis leads to secondary adrenal insufficiency.
Incorrect: Lactotroph necrosis causes hypoprolactinemia, not hyperprolactinemia.
Incorrect: Hypoestrogenism causes endometrial atrophy, not hyperplasia.
questions.explanation: Adrenal insufficiency Explanation: • Loss of ACTH → secondary adrenal insufficiency (low cortisol, normal aldosterone). • Other features: hypothyroidism (low TSH), fatigue, weight loss, hypotension.

questions.case_context: A 24-year-old G2P2 woman delivered vaginally eight months ago. Her pregnancy was uncomplicated, but her delivery was complicated by postpartum hemorrhage requiring uterine curettage and transfusion of four units of packed red blood cells. She complains of amenorrhea since delivery. She was unable to breastfeed her baby. She denies headaches, visual changes, or medication use. Pregnancy test is negative.
questions.stem: Which of the following is consistent with her presumed diagnosis?
options: Usually associated with hypertensive crisis at or soon after a delivery
Caused by an ischemic necrosis of the posterior pituitary gland
Often associated with elevated TSH levels
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Sheehan syndrome is caused by hemorrhagic hypotension/hypovolemic shock, not hypertensive crisis.
Incorrect: It involves ischemic necrosis of the anterior pituitary (posterior pituitary has separate arterial supply).
Correct: Lactotroph infarction leads to decreased prolactin levels and inability to breastfeed.
Incorrect: Loss of thyrotrophs causes low/inappropriately normal TSH, not elevated TSH.
questions.explanation: Associated with decreased prolactin levels Explanation: • Sheehan syndrome involves ischemic necrosis of the anterior pituitary, not the posterior pituitary (so B is incorrect). • It is associated with low prolactin, explaining inability to lactate. • TSH is low, not elevated (D incorrect). • Hypertensive crisis is not the cause; the cause is hypovolemic shock from postpartum hemorrhage (A incorrect).

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which chromosomal abnormality is characteristic of testicular germ cell tumors?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: t(14;18) is characteristic of follicular lymphoma.
Correct: Isochromosome 12p [i(12p)] is the characteristic chromosomal abnormality of testicular germ cell tumors.
Incorrect: t(9;22) (Philadelphia chromosome) is characteristic of CML.
Incorrect: Monosomy X is Turner syndrome.
Incorrect: Trisomy 21 is Down syndrome.
questions.explanation: Isochromosome 12p Explanation: • Isochromosome 12p [i(12p)] is the characteristic chromosomal abnormality of testicular germ cell tumors. • t(14;18) is follicular lymphoma and t(9;22) is chronic myeloid leukemia, while trisomy 21 and monosomy X are constitutional syndromes.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which breast lesion is most likely to present as a stellate lesion with central sclerosis and mimic carcinoma on imaging?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Fibroadenoma presents as a well-circumscribed oval mass, not a stellate lesion.
Correct: Radial scar is a benign sclerosing breast lesion with a stellate appearance and central sclerosis that closely mimics invasive carcinoma on mammography.
Incorrect: Phyllodes tumor presents as a well-circumscribed lobulated mass.
Incorrect: Papilloma presents within a dilated duct, often with nipple discharge.
Incorrect: DCIS typically presents as microcalcifications.
questions.explanation: Radial scar Explanation: • Radial scar is a benign sclerosing breast lesion with a stellate appearance and central sclerosis that closely mimics invasive carcinoma on mammography. • Because radial scar can mimic invasive carcinoma, biopsy or excision is needed to establish the diagnosis.

questions.case_context: A 16-year-old girl presents with primary amenorrhea and cyclic pelvic pain. Physical exam shows normal secondary sexual characteristics and a bulging bluish membrane at the vaginal introitus.
questions.stem: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
choice_rationales: Correct: Imperforate hymen causes primary amenorrhea with cyclic pelvic pain and a bulging bluish membrane (hematocolpos) with normal secondary sexual characteristics.
Incorrect: Müllerian agenesis lacks a uterus and menses, so there is no cyclic hematocolpos or bulging bluish membrane.
Incorrect: Androgen insensitivity syndrome has an absent uterus and scant pubic/axillary hair.
Incorrect: Hypothalamic amenorrhea causes anovulation without outflow obstruction or hematocolpos.
questions.explanation: Imperforate hymen Explanation: • Cyclic pelvic pain with a bulging bluish membrane at the introitus reflects retained menstrual blood (hematocolpos) behind an imperforate hymen, with normal secondary sexual characteristics. • Müllerian agenesis and androgen insensitivity have no uterus and no cyclic bleeding, and hypothalamic amenorrhea has no outflow obstruction.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which ovarian tumor is most commonly associated with hyperthyroidism?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Dysgerminoma is a germ cell tumor that does not produce thyroid hormone.
Correct: Struma ovarii is a specialized ovarian teratoma composed predominantly of thyroid tissue, which can cause hyperthyroidism.
Incorrect: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors produce androgens (virilization).
Incorrect: Granulosa cell tumors produce estrogen.
Incorrect: Yolk sac tumors produce AFP.
questions.explanation: Struma ovarii Explanation: • Struma ovarii is a specialized ovarian teratoma composed predominantly of thyroid tissue, which can cause hyperthyroidism. • Most cases are benign, and the thyroid tissue can produce excess thyroid hormone.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which mixed tumor contains both malignant epithelial and stromal components?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Adenofibroma is a benign mixed epithelial-stromal tumor.
Correct: Malignant mixed Müllerian tumor (MMMT / carcinosarcoma) contains both malignant epithelial (carcinomatous) and malignant stromal (sarcomatous) components.
Incorrect: Brenner tumor is a benign transitional-cell ovarian tumor.
Incorrect: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor is a sex cord–stromal tumor.
Incorrect: Granulosa cell tumor is a sex cord–stromal tumor.
questions.explanation: MMMT Explanation: • Malignant mixed Müllerian tumor (MMMT / carcinosarcoma) contains both malignant epithelial (carcinomatous) and malignant stromal (sarcomatous) components. • It is also called carcinosarcoma and occurs mainly in postmenopausal women, while adenofibroma is a benign tumor with epithelial and stromal parts.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: A 60-year-old man has elevated PSA and a firm nodule on digital rectal examination (DRE). Biopsy shows small crowded glands lacking basal cells. Which immunostain confirms malignancy?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Inhibin stains sex cord–stromal tumors, not prostatic adenocarcinoma.
Correct: AMACR (P504S) is overexpressed in prostatic adenocarcinoma, confirming malignancy in small crowded glands lacking p63+ basal cells.
Incorrect: p63 stains benign basal cells, which are ABSENT in prostatic adenocarcinoma.
Incorrect: PSA confirms prostatic origin (both benign and malignant), not malignancy itself.
Incorrect: Ki-67 is a general proliferation marker, not a diagnostic prostate malignancy immunostain.
questions.explanation: AMACR (P504S) Explanation: • Prostatic adenocarcinoma shows small crowded glands that lack a basal cell layer, so basal cell markers such as p63 are negative. • AMACR (P504S) is overexpressed in malignant prostatic glands and confirms malignancy.

questions.stem: What is the role of the Sertoli cells in the male reproductive system during puberty?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Testosterone is produced by Leydig cells under LH stimulation, not by Sertoli cells.
Correct: Sertoli cells support and nourish developing germ cells, enabling sperm production.
Incorrect: Sertoli cells give negative feedback to FSH through inhibin B, not positive feedback.
Incorrect: Leydig cells are stimulated by LH, and Sertoli cells are not their primary regulator.
