questions.explanation: Production of sperm Explanation: • Sertoli cells line the seminiferous tubules and, under FSH and testosterone, support and nourish developing germ cells to enable spermatogenesis. • They also secrete inhibin B, which gives negative feedback to FSH, and form the blood testis barrier. • Testosterone is made by Leydig cells.

questions.stem: What outcome may occur if precocious puberty in a girl is not diagnosed and treated?
options: Premature growth plate closure and stature shorter than expected
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Macromastia is not a recognized outcome of untreated precocious puberty.
Correct: Early sex steroid exposure causes premature growth plate closure and a shorter final height.
Incorrect: Precocious puberty leads to early menarche, not late menarche.
Incorrect: Acne can occur with early androgen exposure but is not the key long term outcome of untreated precocious puberty.
questions.explanation: Premature growth plate closure and stature shorter than expected Explanation: • Early exposure to sex steroids accelerates growth at first but causes early epiphyseal fusion. • Untreated precocious puberty therefore leads to a shorter final adult height than expected.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old G1P0 woman presents for her first prenatal visit at 10 weeks gestation. Her blood pressure is 146/92 mm Hg on two separate readings taken four hours apart. She denies any history of hypertension prior to pregnancy. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnosis?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Gestational hypertension is diagnosed at 20 weeks gestation or later.
Incorrect: Preeclampsia typically develops at 20 weeks or later (except with a molar pregnancy) with proteinuria or end organ signs.
Correct: Hypertension of 140/90 mm Hg or higher present before 20 weeks gestation, here at 10 weeks, is chronic hypertension.
Incorrect: Transient hypertension of pregnancy is an older term for late pregnancy blood pressure elevation that resolves after delivery, not hypertension already present at 10 weeks.
Incorrect: White coat hypertension is elevated clinic blood pressure with normal readings outside the clinic, and these persistent readings four hours apart support true hypertension.
questions.explanation: Chronic hypertension Explanation: • Hypertension of 140/90 mm Hg or higher that is present before 20 weeks gestation is classified as chronic hypertension. • Gestational hypertension and preeclampsia are defined by onset at or after 20 weeks.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which infection is associated with strawberry cervix?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Candida causes thick cottage-cheese discharge and pseudohyphae, not strawberry cervix.
Correct: Trichomonas vaginalis causes punctate cervical hemorrhages ('strawberry cervix') and frothy, malodorous yellow-green discharge.
Incorrect: HSV causes painful vesicular/ulcerative lesions.
Incorrect: HPV causes condylomata acuminata and cervical dysplasia.
Incorrect: Gardnerella (bacterial vaginosis) causes thin gray discharge, fishy odor, and clue cells without inflammation.
questions.explanation: Trichomonas vaginalis Explanation: • Trichomonas vaginalis causes punctate cervical hemorrhages ('strawberry cervix') and frothy, malodorous yellow-green discharge. • Trichomonas is a flagellated protozoan seen as motile trophozoites on wet mount and is treated with metronidazole.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which ovarian tumor is most likely to cause pseudomyxoma peritonei?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Serous cystadenocarcinoma produces watery/serous fluid and psammoma bodies, not mucinous ascites.
Correct: Ovarian mucinous cystadenocarcinoma (along with appendiceal mucinous neoplasms) can rupture and seed the peritoneum with mucin-producing cells, causing pseudomyxoma peritonei.
Incorrect: Dysgerminoma is a solid germ cell tumor.
Incorrect: Clear cell carcinoma does not cause pseudomyxoma peritonei.
Incorrect: Ovarian fibroma is associated with Meigs syndrome, not pseudomyxoma peritonei.
questions.explanation: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma Explanation: • Ovarian mucinous cystadenocarcinoma (along with appendiceal mucinous neoplasms) can rupture and seed the peritoneum with mucin-producing cells, causing pseudomyxoma peritonei. • Serous tumors are the most common epithelial ovarian neoplasms but do not produce the abundant mucin that causes this condition.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the relationship between gestational hypertension and preeclampsia?
options: Gestational hypertension always progresses to preeclampsia.
Gestational hypertension is a form of preeclampsia.
Gestational hypertension may progress to preeclampsia in some patients.
Gestational hypertension and preeclampsia are unrelated conditions.
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Many patients with gestational hypertension never progress to preeclampsia.
Incorrect: Gestational hypertension lacks proteinuria and severe features, distinguishing it from preeclampsia.
Correct: Gestational hypertension may progress to preeclampsia in a subset of patients, warranting close monitoring.
Incorrect: They lie on the same spectrum of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
questions.explanation: Gestational hypertension may progress to preeclampsia in some patients Explanation: Gestational hypertension can progress to preeclampsia, especially if severe-range blood pressures develop.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old G1P0 woman at 36 weeks gestation is admitted for evaluation of severe preeclampsia. Her blood pressure is 170/115 mm Hg, and she reports a persistent frontal headache and visual disturbances. While being monitored in the labor and delivery unit, she suddenly develops generalized tonic-clonic seizures lasting approximately 90 seconds. After the seizure resolves, she is confused and somnolent. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
options: Intubate and transfer to the ICU
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Benzodiazepines (diazepam) are not first-line for eclamptic seizure prophylaxis/treatment.
Incorrect: Delivery is definitive, but maternal stabilization with magnesium sulfate must occur first to prevent recurrent seizures.
Correct: Intravenous magnesium sulfate is the first-line treatment for eclampsia to stop/prevent recurrent seizures and stabilize the mother.
Incorrect: Intubation is reserved for airway compromise or respiratory failure.
Incorrect: Phenytoin is inferior to magnesium sulfate for eclampsia.
questions.explanation: Administer intravenous magnesium sulfate Explanation: This patient has developed eclampsia, defined as new-onset seizures in a woman with preeclampsia. The first-line treatment is magnesium sulfate, which prevents further seizures and stabilizes the patient. Delivery is the definitive treatment for preeclampsia/eclampsia, but magnesium sulfate must be administered first to prevent recurrent seizures and stabilize the mother before delivery. • Diazepam and phenytoin are not first-line treatments for eclampsia. • Emergent cesarean delivery may be necessary, but only after maternal stabilization. • Intubation is reserved for patients with compromised airway or respiratory failure.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which testicular tumor is most commonly associated with precocious puberty in boys?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Seminoma occurs in adult men and does not cause precocious puberty.
Correct: Leydig cell tumors secrete androgens (testosterone), classically causing isosexual precocious puberty in boys.
Incorrect: Sertoli cell tumors are usually hormonally silent or occasionally feminizing.
Incorrect: Embryonal carcinoma occurs in young adults.
Incorrect: Teratomas do not typically secrete androgens.
questions.explanation: Leydig cell tumor Explanation: • Leydig cell tumors secrete androgens (testosterone), classically causing isosexual precocious puberty in boys. • Leydig cell tumors contain Reinke crystals and in adults can cause gynecomastia.

questions.stem: A 15 year old boy with obesity presents with visible but small bilateral breasts. On examination, no glandular tissue is palpable in the breasts. He likely has:
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Precocious puberty means pubertal onset at an early age, and a 15 year old boy is within the normal pubertal range.
Correct: Visible breast enlargement from fat with no palpable glandular tissue in an obese boy is pseudogynecomastia.
Incorrect: Gynecomastia requires palpable glandular tissue, which is absent on this exam.
Incorrect: A hypothalamic tumor can cause central precocious puberty but does not explain fat deposition without glandular tissue.
questions.explanation: Pseudogynecomastia Explanation: • Pseudogynecomastia is excess fat deposition in the chest, common in obesity, with no palpable glandular tissue. • True gynecomastia has palpable, firm glandular tissue under the nipple. • Precocious puberty and hypothalamic tumors would not explain a boy this age having breast fat without glandular tissue.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman at 37 weeks gestation is diagnosed with gestational hypertension. Her blood pressure is 142/92 mm Hg. She is asymptomatic and has no proteinuria. What is the next best step in management?
options: Continue expectant management with close monitoring
Administer corticosteroids for fetal lung maturity
choice_rationales: Correct: At 37 weeks gestation (term), delivery is indicated for gestational hypertension without severe features per ACOG guidelines.
Incorrect: Magnesium sulfate is not indicated for gestational hypertension without severe features.
Incorrect: Expectant management with close monitoring is appropriate before 37 weeks gestation, not at ≥37 weeks term.
Incorrect: Antenatal corticosteroids are used <34 weeks (or selected late preterm cases), not at 37 weeks term.
questions.explanation: A. Immediate delivery — Per ACOG guidelines, delivery is recommended at ≥37 0/7 weeks gestation for gestational hypertension without severe features (expectant management is reserved for <37 weeks). (Corrected from source PDF key C.)

questions.case_context: A 32-year-old G1P1 woman presents with an eight-month history of amenorrhea. A pregnancy test is negative. TSH and prolactin levels are normal. The FSH level is elevated at 40 IU/L.
questions.stem: Which of the following is the most likely complication for this patient?
options: She is at significant risk for endometrial cancer
She is at increased risk for ovarian cancer
She is at increased risk for osteoporosis
She is at increased risk for multiple gestation
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Endometrial cancer is driven by unopposed estrogen, whereas POI causes hypoestrogenism.
Incorrect: POI does not increase ovarian cancer risk.
Correct: Elevated FSH (40 IU/L) indicates premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) and hypoestrogenism, accelerating bone loss and increasing osteoporosis risk.
Incorrect: Multiple gestation is associated with ovulation induction, not spontaneous POI.
questions.explanation: She is at increased risk for osteoporosis Explanation: • Elevated FSH indicates premature ovarian insufficiency (POI), leading to hypoestrogenism. Low estrogen accelerates bone loss, increasing the risk of osteoporosis. • A is incorrect because endometrial cancer risk is associated with unopposed estrogen, not hypoestrogenism. • B is incorrect because POI does not increase ovarian cancer risk. • D is incorrect because multiple gestation risk is linked to ovulation induction, not spontaneous POI.

questions.case_context: A 32-year-old G1P1 woman presents with an eight-month history of amenorrhea. A pregnancy test is negative. TSH and prolactin levels are normal. The FSH level is elevated at 40 IU/L.
questions.stem: If the patient above (32-year-old woman with amenorrhea and elevated FSH) were to have a diagnostic workup, which of the following is most likely to be noted?
options: No bleeding with a progestin challenge test
choice_rationales: Incorrect: An obliterated uterine cavity on HSG is seen in Asherman syndrome, where FSH is normal.
Correct: Because POI causes hypoestrogenism, the endometrium is unprimed and does not bleed after a progestin challenge test.
Incorrect: Estradiol is low, not normal, in POI.
Incorrect: Brain MRI is normal in POI (the defect is ovarian, not pituitary/hypothalamic).
questions.explanation: No bleeding with a progestin challenge test Explanation: • C -- The patient has premature ovarian insufficiency (POI), indicated by elevated FSH (40 IU/L). In POI, estradiol levels are low, not normal. • A suggests Asherman syndrome (intrauterine adhesions), which is not the case here. • D would indicate a pituitary or hypothalamic lesion, but TSH and prolactin are normal, making this unlikely.

questions.stem: Which hormone is responsible for the development of pubic hair?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Testosterone contributes to androgen effects, but the adrenal androgen DHEAS is the hormone credited with pubic hair development in this question.
Incorrect: Estrogen drives breast development and is not the hormone responsible for pubic hair.
Incorrect: LH acts on the gonads and does not act directly on pubic hair follicles.
Correct: DHEAS, an adrenal androgen, drives pubic hair development (pubarche).
questions.explanation: DHEAS Explanation: • Adrenarche is the rise in adrenal androgens (DHEA and DHEAS) from the zona reticularis. • These adrenal androgens drive pubic and axillary hair growth (pubarche) and body odor. • LH and estrogen act through the gonads and breast rather than directly on pubic hair.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which of the following is the most important prognostic factor in urothelial carcinoma?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Tumor size is less predictive than depth of invasion into the lamina propria or muscularis propria.
Incorrect: Mitotic rate reflects grade but is secondary to invasion depth.
Correct: Extent/depth of invasion (especially muscularis propria invasion) is the most important prognostic factor in urothelial carcinoma.
Incorrect: Necrosis is not the primary prognostic determinant.
Incorrect: Cytologic atypia determines grade, whereas depth of invasion drives staging and prognosis.
questions.explanation: Extent of invasion Explanation: • Extent/depth of invasion (especially muscularis propria invasion) is the most important prognostic factor in urothelial carcinoma. • Depth of invasion determines the stage, including whether disease is non muscle invasive or muscle invasive, which guides treatment.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: A patient presents with an eczematous lesion of the nipple and underlying ductal carcinoma in situ. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
choice_rationales: Correct: Paget disease of the breast presents as an eczematous, crusted nipple lesion caused by intraepidermal extension of underlying DCIS.
Incorrect: Paget disease of the vulva occurs on the vulva and is usually not associated with underlying carcinoma.
Incorrect: LCIS is an incidental microscopic lobular finding without nipple eczema.
Incorrect: Invasive ductal carcinoma typically presents as a palpable mass or mammographic density rather than isolated nipple eczema.
Incorrect: Medullary carcinoma presents as a well-circumscribed breast mass.
questions.explanation: Paget disease of the breast Explanation: • Paget disease of the breast presents as an eczematous, crusted nipple lesion caused by intraepidermal extension of underlying DCIS. • Paget cells are large cells with abundant pale cytoplasm within the epidermis, and an underlying DCIS or invasive carcinoma is usually present.

questions.case_context: An 18-year-old nulliparous adolescent woman complains that she has not yet started menstruating. She denies weight loss or excessive exercise. Each of her sisters achieved menarche by 13 years of age. Her mother recalls a doctor mentioning that her daughter had a missing right kidney on an abdominal x-ray. On examination: • Height: 5’6”, Weight: 140 lbs • BP: 110/60 mmHg • Thyroid: Normal • Tanner stage IV breasts, female external genitalia, Tanner stage IV axillary and pubic hair • No skin lesions
questions.stem: What is the most likely diagnosis?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Turner syndrome has absent breast development and short stature with webbed neck.
Incorrect: Androgen insensitivity syndrome has scant/absent pubic and axillary hair.
Correct: Normal breasts, normal pubic/axillary hair, primary amenorrhea, absent uterus, and unilateral renal agenesis are classic for Müllerian agenesis (MRKH syndrome).
Incorrect: Hypothalamic amenorrhea has a normal uterus and normal renal anatomy.
questions.explanation: Müllerian agenesis (MRKH syndrome) Explanation: • Primary amenorrhea with normal secondary sexual characteristics and normal androgen-dependent hair suggests normal ovarian function but absent uterus. • Associated renal anomalies (missing kidney) strongly point to MRKH syndrome.

questions.case_context: An 18-year-old nulliparous adolescent woman complains that she has not yet started menstruating. She denies weight loss or excessive exercise. Each of her sisters achieved menarche by 13 years of age. Her mother recalls a doctor mentioning that her daughter had a missing right kidney on an abdominal x-ray. On examination: • Height: 5’6”, Weight: 140 lbs • BP: 110/60 mmHg • Thyroid: Normal • Tanner stage IV breasts, female external genitalia, Tanner stage IV axillary and pubic hair • No skin lesions
questions.stem: What is the next step in diagnosis?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Karyotype (46,XX) is normal in MRKH and is usually checked alongside or after imaging confirms absent uterus.
Correct: Pelvic ultrasound or MRI is the next step to confirm absence of the uterus and upper vagina (and evaluate ovaries/kidneys).
Incorrect: FSH and LH are normal in MRKH because ovarian function is intact.
Incorrect: Progesterone challenge is unnecessary/uninformative when anatomic absence of the uterus is suspected.
questions.explanation: Pelvic ultrasound or MRI Explanation: • Imaging confirms absence of uterus and upper vagina. • Karyotype is usually 46,XX in MRKH syndrome.

questions.case_context: An 18-year-old nulliparous adolescent woman complains that she has not yet started menstruating. She denies weight loss or excessive exercise. Each of her sisters achieved menarche by 13 years of age. Her mother recalls a doctor mentioning that her daughter had a missing right kidney on an abdominal x-ray. On examination: • Height: 5’6”, Weight: 140 lbs • BP: 110/60 mmHg • Thyroid: Normal • Tanner stage IV breasts, female external genitalia, Tanner stage IV axillary and pubic hair • No skin lesions
questions.stem: What is the most likely finding on pelvic examination?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: The uterus and cervix fail to develop from the paramesonephric (Müllerian) ducts.
Correct: Because the lower vagina derives from the urogenital sinus while the upper vagina and uterus fail to develop, pelvic exam reveals a blind-ending vaginal pouch.
Incorrect: Ovaries are present and functional in MRKH; the uterus is absent.
Incorrect: External genitalia are normal female.
questions.explanation: Blind-ending vaginal pouch Explanation: • External genitalia are normal, but the vagina ends blindly because the uterus and upper vagina fail to develop.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: Which bladder tumor is associated with Schistosoma haematobium infection?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Urothelial carcinoma is the most common bladder cancer overall (linked to smoking, aromatic amines), not Schistosoma.
Incorrect: Bladder adenocarcinoma is associated with urachal remnants or bladder exstrophy.
Incorrect: Small cell carcinoma of the bladder is rare and neuroendocrine.
Correct: Chronic Schistosoma haematobium infection causes squamous metaplasia of the bladder urothelium, predisposing to squamous cell carcinoma.
Incorrect: Sarcoma is a rare mesenchymal bladder tumor.
questions.explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma Explanation: • Chronic Schistosoma haematobium infection causes squamous metaplasia of the bladder urothelium, predisposing to squamous cell carcinoma. • Urothelial carcinoma is the most common bladder cancer overall, but schistosomiasis specifically predisposes to squamous cell carcinoma.

questions.case_context: A 41-year-old woman is suspected of having uterine adhesions (Asherman syndrome) because she has had irregular menses since a spontaneous abortion 18 months previously.
questions.stem: Which of the following historical or laboratory pieces of information would support this diagnosis?
options: FSH level too low to be measurable
Normal estradiol levels in a reproductive-aged woman
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Hot flashes indicate hypoestrogenism (e.g., POI/menopause), not Asherman syndrome.
Incorrect: Undetectably low FSH indicates hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, whereas Asherman has normal FSH.
Correct: In Asherman syndrome, ovarian function and the HPO axis remain intact, so estradiol levels are normal for a reproductive-aged woman.
Incorrect: Monophasic BBT indicates anovulation, whereas women with Asherman syndrome continue to ovulate normally (biphasic BBT).
questions.explanation: Normal estradiol levels in a reproductive-aged woman Explanation: • In Asherman syndrome, the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis is intact, so estrogen production remains normal. The amenorrhea is due to endometrial scarring, not hormonal deficiency. • A (hot flashes) and B (low FSH) suggest ovarian failure or hypothalamic dysfunction, which is not the case here. • D (monophasic BBT) indicates anovulation, which is not typical in Asherman syndrome because ovulation usually continues.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 24 weeks gestation comes for a routine prenatal visit. Which of the following best describes the normal physiological change in plasma volume during pregnancy?
options: Plasma volume decreases due to increased renal clearance
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Plasma volume expands rather than decreases during pregnancy.
Incorrect: Plasma volume increases substantially.
Incorrect: A 20% increase underestimates the physiologic expansion (and is closer to the smaller rise in red cell mass).
Correct: Plasma volume increases by approximately 40–50% during pregnancy to support uteroplacental perfusion, contributing to physiologic anemia of pregnancy.
Incorrect: Increased renal clearance (GFR) does not reduce plasma volume.
questions.explanation: Plasma volume increases by approximately 40–50% Explanation: • During pregnancy, plasma volume expands significantly (about 40–50%) to support uteroplacental circulation and fetal growth. • This increase contributes to physiologic anemia of pregnancy because red cell mass increases less than plasma volume. • Cardiac output also rises, and systemic vascular resistance falls due to progesterone-mediated vasodilation.

questions.stem: In males, what is the main role of Leydig cells during puberty?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Sperm are produced in the seminiferous tubules with support from Sertoli cells.
Incorrect: DHEAS is produced by the adrenal cortex, not by Leydig cells.
Correct: Leydig cells produce testosterone in response to LH.
Incorrect: FSH is produced by anterior pituitary gonadotrophs, not by Leydig cells.
questions.explanation: Production of testosterone Explanation: • Leydig cells sit in the interstitium between seminiferous tubules and make testosterone when stimulated by LH. • Sertoli cells, not Leydig cells, support spermatogenesis. • DHEAS comes from the adrenal cortex and FSH comes from the anterior pituitary.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman at 32 weeks gestation presents for a routine prenatal visit. Blood pressure on previous visits was 100-110/60-72. Her blood pressure today is 148/92 mm Hg. She has no complaints. Urinalysis shows no proteinuria. Repeat BP later that day is 150/90. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnosis?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Pre-pregnancy/early-pregnancy BPs were normal (100–110/60–72), ruling out chronic hypertension.
Correct: New-onset hypertension (≥140/90 mmHg on two occasions) after 20 weeks gestation without proteinuria or severe features is gestational hypertension.
Incorrect: Preeclampsia requires proteinuria or severe end-organ features, which are absent here.
Incorrect: BP is <160/110 and there are no severe features.
questions.explanation: Gestational hypertension Explanation: Gestational hypertension is defined as new-onset hypertension (≥140/90 mm Hg) after 20 weeks gestation without proteinuria or severe features.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old G2P1 woman at 36 weeks gestation presents with severe preeclampsia. Her blood pressure is 172/112 mm Hg, confirmed on two readings 20 minutes apart. She is alert and oriented, with no signs of eclampsia. Which of the following medications is most appropriate for initial management of her blood pressure?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Methyldopa has a slow onset and is not used for acute severe hypertension (≥160/110 mmHg).
Correct: Immediate-release oral nifedipine (along with IV labetalol or IV hydralazine) is a first-line agent for acute severe hypertension in pregnancy.
Incorrect: Magnesium sulfate is given for seizure prophylaxis, not as primary antihypertensive therapy.
Incorrect: Enalapril (ACE inhibitor) is contraindicated in pregnancy due to fetal toxicity.
Incorrect: Furosemide is not first-line for acute preeclampsia BP control and can worsen intravascular volume depletion.
questions.explanation: Oral nifedipine Explanation: • Blood pressure of 160/110 mm Hg or higher that persists in pregnancy is a hypertensive emergency and should be treated within 30 to 60 minutes. • First line agents are IV labetalol, IV hydralazine, or immediate release oral nifedipine. • Magnesium sulfate prevents seizures but is not an antihypertensive, and ACE inhibitors are contraindicated in pregnancy.

questions.lecture_title: R18 Pathology of Breast & Reproductive Diseases
questions.stem: A 35-year-old man undergoes orchiectomy for a testicular mass. Histology reveals syncytiotrophoblasts and cytotrophoblasts. Which serum marker is most likely elevated?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: AFP is elevated in yolk sac tumor, not pure choriocarcinoma.
Correct: Syncytiotrophoblasts produce β-hCG, which is markedly elevated in testicular choriocarcinoma.
Incorrect: LDH is a nonspecific marker of tumor burden (often elevated in seminoma).
Incorrect: PLAP is classically positive in seminoma.
Incorrect: CA-19-9 is a gastrointestinal/pancreatic tumor marker.
questions.explanation: β-hCG Explanation: • Syncytiotrophoblasts produce β-hCG, which is markedly elevated in testicular choriocarcinoma. • AFP is raised in yolk sac tumor, while LDH and PLAP are nonspecific markers of germ cell tumors such as seminoma.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common testicular tumor in infants and young children?
choice_rationales: Incorrect: Seminoma is the most common testicular tumor in young adult men, not infants/young children.
Incorrect: Embryonal carcinoma occurs in young adults (20–30 years).
Correct: Yolk sac tumor (endodermal sinus tumor) is the most common testicular tumor in infants and young children.
Incorrect: Teratoma is the second most common in children, behind yolk sac tumor.
Incorrect: Choriocarcinoma occurs primarily in young adult men.
questions.explanation: Yolk sac tumor Explanation: • Yolk sac tumor (endodermal sinus tumor) is the most common testicular tumor in infants and young children. • Prepubertal yolk sac tumors typically show Schiller-Duval bodies and elevated AFP.
